name: epanet_equipment_line
description: An equipment item rated 50 kPa at 15 L/s (water at 15 C) between two reservoirs, as an EPANET TCV of the same K on its inlet pipe's bore: verifies the element's square law and the line's flow and heads against EPANET 2.2.
source: WNTR 1.5.0 EpanetSimulator (EPANET 2.2.0); see tests/reference/generate_epanet_cases.py. D-W headloss, GPM INP units, accuracy 1e-5, headerror 1e-9 ft and flowchange 1e-12 gpm (EPANET reads both in the INP units, input1.c:595-596; WNTR writes them unconverted); viscosity VISCOS = 1.1e-5 ft2/s = 1.02193344e-6 m2/s (the project's custom fluid has the same nu; its density, 1000 kg/m3, does not affect the comparison because friction depends only on nu and a surface-pressure head p/(rho g) is converted with the same rho and g on both sides); solver run in 'swamee_jain' mode. Known EPANET biases, all far inside the 0.5% criterion: EPANET's head-loss coefficients use g = 32.2 ft/s2 = 9.81456 m/s2 against our 9.80665 (0.08% in head loss), its minor-loss constant is 0.02517 against the exact 1/(2g(pi/4)^2) = 0.0251730 in US units (0.012%), its GPM flow-unit constant GPMperCFS = 448.831 differs from the exact ft3/(gal/60) by -3.8e-07 (relative, in flow), and its results are float32 (about 1e-7 relative). Equipment: EPANET TCV between junctions at its ports' elevations, diameter of the inlet pipe, minor loss 0, setting K_E = 2 g A^2 c on that bore (2 dP_r A^2/(rho_r Q_r^2) for a rated point; for a Cv or Kv the K of that coefficient on the inlet bore by its definition, element_laws.k_from_flow_coefficient), written by WNTR with 11 significant digits; EPANET's TCV loss is 0.02517 K/d^4 in ft with g = 32.2 ft/s2, 0.99908 of ours (network_check.EPANET_MODEL). Expected equipment results from EPANET's flow and heads: loss rho g (H_in - H_out), static drop with v in each port's pipe.
